evidence.summary: Review rework (duplicate claim metadata): from_packet() now judges each duplicate entry on its own metadata, selects the kept entry by a total order (permissiveness, restricted first, kind, status, usage, text, attribution) instead of input position, merges safety flags pessimistically and records any disagreement on producer kind/status/usage/flags in ResearchItem.metadata_conflicts, which restricts the claim. Tests permute every ordering (including entries split across both claim lists) and assert identical results, never-more-permissive, and a recorded conflict. Mutation checks: ignoring the conflict, restoring the order-dependent selection, taking flags from the first entry and not recording kind conflicts each fail tests.

Also from the review: the research digest additionally covers claim text, attribution, source ids and duplicate conflicts, and is carried and validated by the editor view (brief and view fail on a changed digest even without the brief). Old 0.2 documents are rejected by validation and load().

Tracker transition evidence: checkpoint commit 2da5ad8897969bddc5905d2c3c429d056f0b6e6f holds S-CRD-001-01 IN_PROGRESS and the final branch holds READY_FOR_REVIEW. The integrator's history-aware checker validates every committed tracker snapshot from the branch fork point through HEAD, including the merge of newer origin/main, then the working tree. It preserves the legal PLANNED -> IN_PROGRESS -> READY_FOR_REVIEW sequence and rejects skipped intermediate states; no waiver or transition-graph change is used. orchestrator/creative_director/README.md documents the fail-closed behavior, preserved fields, restrictions, duplicate resolution, the mirrored producer rule and its manual synchronization risk, the digest and its limits, hook rules and the schema version bump.
